title: At BATS, organic carbon and total nitrogen do not close the oxygen budget on density 26.5 in joint 1999-2025 samples
abstract: We test whether conversion of organic material already present can explain the BATS oxygen loss on density 26.5. Joint good oxygen, organic carbon, total nitrogen and nitrate samples compare five supported years in 1999-2008 with all ten years in 2016-2025. AOU rose 13.09 umol/kg, organic carbon fell 1.27 and total nitrogen rose 0.89. At an oxygen to carbon ratio of 1.45, the carbon stock decrease corresponds to 14.1% of the AOU rise, with a conditional temporal interval of 5.8-21.1%. The change in carbon minus oxygen divided by 1.45 is +6.84 [5.26, 8.45] umol C/kg. Eight sampling variants retain the signs. Thus the tested closed retained-pool budget does not close. Continuing organic input, source changes, transport and changed oxygen disequilibrium remain possible. A common-cruise deep calibration control lacks early support. Sparse early years, interpolation and untested calibration drift limit this local concentration test; it is not a bound on respiration supplied by continuing input. Code, annual aggregates, source hashes, support failures and retrieval instructions are included.
